targetReport.title: Council Tax Valuation List
targetReport.description: SPLIT 2026-10-18 (Thomas: 'split gb-voa-rating-lists into the Council Tax Valuation List and the Local Non-Domestic Rating List'): until then one node bundled both VOA lists under the title 'Local Non-Domestic Rating List / Council Tax Valuation List', against the one-node-per-document ruling (2026-10-05), and its own release_schedule note flagged it. The Valuation Office Agency's lists placing every domestic property in England and Wales in a Council Tax band: 1 April 1991 values in England, 1 April 2003 in Wales. They are maintained continuously and altered as properties change. HM Land Registry's UK House Price Index takes its England and Wales property attributes from it. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY in the August 2026 round (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Finance Act 1992 ss.20-23. The url is GOV.UK's 'Check your Council Tax band' service, the list's public face; it links its service as 'on the Council Tax valuation list'.
targetReport.cadence_note: Maintained continuously, with no fixed revaluation cycle in England (Wales is legislating for a revaluation). 1 is a nominal rate, as the bundled node had.

The VOA has been responsible for banding properties for Council Tax since the tax was first introduced in 1993; before then, the VOA was responsible for the earlier system of domestic rates.

targetReport.title: Handbook on Residential Property Prices Indices (RPPIs)
targetReport.publisher: Eurostat, ILO, IMF, OECD, UNECE and the World Bank
targetReport.description: The international methodological handbook for residential property (house) price indices, 2013 edition, published by Eurostat (catalogue KS-RA-12-022) and copyrighted jointly by the European Union, the International Labour Organization, the International Monetary Fund, the OECD, the UN Economic Commission for Europe and the World Bank. It covers the uses of RPPIs, stratification, hedonic regression, repeat-sales and appraisal-based methods, the land/structures split, data sources and recommendations. The publisher's own title spells it 'Prices Indices'; citing documents usually write 'Price Indices'. Minted 2026-10-17 as the hub of the housing research lane.
targetReport.cadence_note: One edition so far (2013); 0.05 is a once-a-generation revision rate written as a number.

targetReport.title: Local Non-Domestic Rating List
targetReport.description: SPLIT 2026-10-18 (Thomas: 'split gb-voa-rating-lists into the Council Tax Valuation List and the Local Non-Domestic Rating List'): until then one node bundled both VOA lists under the title 'Local Non-Domestic Rating List / Council Tax Valuation List', against the one-node-per-document ruling (2026-10-05), and its own release_schedule note flagged it. This id keeps the business-rates list; the Council Tax list is now `gb-voa-council-tax-valuation-list`. The Valuation Office Agency's rating lists of non-domestic properties and their rateable values, the base on which business rates are charged. Compiled at each revaluation and in force from 1 April of the revaluation year: 2023, then 2026, every three years under the Non-Domestic Rating Act 2023. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY in the August 2026 round (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Finance Act 1988 ss.41, 61 and Sch.6. The url is the VOA's own rating list downloads page.
targetReport.cadence_note: Compiled at each revaluation, every three years since the Non-Domestic Rating Act 2023 (2023, 2026, next 2029); amended continuously in between. 0.33 is that cycle written as a rate.

results.window:
The Business Rates Retention Scheme which commenced on 1 April 2013
          requires the Cabinet to formally approve the NNDR1 by the 31 January
          immediately preceding the financial year to which it relates. The NNDR1
          contains details of the rateable values shown for the authority's local rating list
          at 31 December and enables the Council to calculate the expected income in
          respect of business rates for the year, a proportion of which the Council has
          retained from 2013/14 onwards. 3.2.
